stem: Bilal camps on a dark moonless hill far from city lights. He sees a faint band of light across the sky and later reads that astronomers found planets revolving around stars other than the Sun.

parts.text: Which claim best organises the Milky Way, other galaxies, exoplanets, and the question of life elsewhere?

options.text: The faint band is the Milky Way, our home galaxy; other galaxies lie beyond it; exoplanets orbit other stars; whether life exists elsewhere is still unknown.
A planet revolving around another star in the Milky Way is itself a galaxy.
The Milky Way Galaxy sits inside the Solar System.
On a moonless night the Milky Way band is equally easy to see from a brightly lit city and from a dark countryside hill.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The Milky Way is our galaxy and can appear as a faint band from a dark site; exoplanets orbit other stars; life elsewhere remains an open question.

teacher.key_rationale: The Milky Way is our galaxy; other galaxies lie beyond it; exoplanets orbit other stars; life elsewhere is unknown. A planet is not a galaxy; the Solar System sits inside the Milky Way; city lights hide the faint band.
